title: Cardiovascular disease and risk
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EX13b#t4 term and clue written for the game; EX13a#t4 term and clue written for the game; EX13a#t1 term and clue written for the game; EX13b#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EX13a#N.5, EX13b#N.3, EX13a#N.11a, EX13b#N.6, EX13b#N.11, EX13b#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Reliability
items.clue: Shown by a finding when repeat studies give similar results.

items.label: Myocardial infarction
items.clue: Death of heart muscle beyond a completely blocked vessel; a heart attack.

items.label: Coronary arteries
items.clue: Vessels branching from the aorta that supply heart muscle with oxygen and glucose.

items.label: Confounding variable
items.clue: A third factor linked to both things being studied, which can make them appear connected.

questions.stem: A blood clot completely occludes a branch of a coronary artery. What is the direct consequence?

options.text: Blood can no longer pass through the chambers of the heart, so the heart stops beating almost at once.
The region of cardiac muscle supplied by that branch is deprived of oxygen and its cells die.
Fat from the diet keeps building up on the surface of the clot until the artery bursts open.
The muscle in the artery wall contracts to force the clot along, tearing the artery wall.

questions.explanation: The coronary arteries supply the cardiac muscle of the heart wall. Occlusion cuts off the oxygen supply to the muscle beyond the block, so the cells there die: a myocardial infarction. The damaged region may then fail to contract properly.

questions.stem: Illustrative data. In a study of 20 countries, the correlation coefficient between mean saturated fat intake and the death rate from coronary heart disease was +0.85. What can be concluded from this result alone?

options.text: There is a strong positive correlation between the variables, but this does not prove that one causes the other.
Saturated fat in the diet is shown to cause coronary heart disease, because the coefficient is so close to +1, the maximum.
The relationship is weak, because a correlation calculated from only 20 countries cannot be a strong one.
Saturated fat from food coats the inside of the coronary arteries, which is why the two variables rise together in step.

questions.stem: A man has atheroma in a carotid artery, which carries blood to the brain. A plaque ruptures. What is most likely to happen next?

options.text: Fat from his blood keeps sticking to the exposed plaque until, over a few hours, the carotid artery bursts open.
The ruptured plaque stops blood passing through the chambers of his heart, so no blood reaches his brain.
The smooth muscle of the artery wall contracts to push the broken plaque along the vessel to his brain.
A clot forms at the rupture and blocks this artery or a smaller one; brain tissue beyond lacks oxygen.

questions.explanation: Same chain as a heart attack: damaged wall → plaque → rupture → clot → occlusion. In the brain, the result is a stroke.

questions.stem: Early epidemiological studies found that women taking HRT had a lower incidence of coronary heart disease (CHD). Later randomised controlled trials found that HRT slightly increased CHD risk. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: The early studies were correct because they involved far more women than the trials did, so their result should be preferred.
The correlation was not causal: women on HRT tended to have higher socioeconomic status, which itself lowers CHD risk.
HRT must lower CHD risk in most women, and the trials must have happened to sample an unusual group of women.
The early correlation must have been a chance result: women on HRT did not really have lower CHD rates.

questions.stem: A woman has a mass of 70 kg and a height of 1.65 m. What is her BMI?

options.text: 25.7 kg m⁻²
21.2 kg m⁻²
42.4 kg m⁻²

questions.stem: Illustrative data. A study of 2000 adults found a correlation coefficient of −0.40 between hours of golf played per week and the incidence of coronary heart disease. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Playing golf probably protects against coronary heart disease, since the correlation shows that more golf goes with less disease.
There is almost no relationship, because a negative coefficient always shows a weak link between two variables.
The relationship must be strong, since it was measured in 2000 people and sample size shows how strong a link is.
More golf goes with less disease, moderately; a confounder such as income may explain it, so cause is not shown.
